title: A cyclotomic ring of integers has an integral power basis
statement: For each integer $N\geq1$ there exists a primitive $N$th root of unity $\zeta\in\mathbf C$, meaning $\zeta^N=1$ and $\zeta^j\neq1$ for $0<j<N$. For any such $\zeta$, let $K=\mathbf Q(\zeta)\subset\mathbf C$ be the smallest subfield containing $\mathbf Q$ and $\zeta$, and let $A=\{a\in K:a\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial in }\mathbf Z[T]\}$ be its ring of integers. Then $K$ is a number field (a finite-dimensional extension of $\mathbf Q$), and $A$ is a free $\mathbf Z$-module with basis $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{d-1}$, where $d=\varphi(N)\geq1$ and $\varphi(N)$ is the number of integers $1\leq j\leq N$ coprime to $N$. Field generation has the meaning of [def-weil-simple-field-extension], the ring of integers is the integral closure of $\mathbf Z$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and a free module and its basis have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Finite-dimensional means spanned by a finite family [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause: Complex.isPrimitiveRoot_exp (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Complex.lean:92-94) gives a primitive root for N nonzero. IsPrimitiveRoot.adjoin_isCyclotomicExtension (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:469) supplies the cyclotomic-extension instance on the algebraic simple adjunction, which is the field Q(zeta); IsCyclotomicExtension.numberField (:410) supplies NumberField K. These are the standard algebraic-adjunction and cyclotomic instances for this specialization, not a claim that C is algebraic over Q. IsPrimitiveRoot.integralPowerBasis (Basic.lean:853-855), integralPowerBasis_gen (:858-862) and integralPowerBasis_dim (:865-867) give the integral power basis with generator zeta and dimension phi(N). PowerBasis.basis_eq_pow (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerBasis.lean:60-64) reads it as the displayed basis. This is the integral basis of O_K, not merely the rational basis of K.
